verses.zh: 以后，他带我到一座门，就是朝东的门。
verses.en: Then he brought me to the gate that faced toward the east.

verses.zh: 以色列　神的荣光从东而来。他的声音如同多水的声音；地就因他的荣耀发光。
verses.en: I saw[NOTE:1] the glory of the God of Israel[NOTE:2] coming from the east;[NOTE:3] the sound was like that of rushing water,[NOTE:4] and the earth radiated[NOTE:5] his glory.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
This same title appears in 8:4; 9:3; 10:19; 11:22.
Earlier Ezekiel had observed God leaving the temple to the east (11:23).
Heb “shone from.”
verses.commentary:
43:2 "the glory of the God of Israel was coming from the way of the east" We must remember that the glory,
or the presence of YHWH, had left, moving east to be with the exiles in Babylon (cf. Ezek. 10:18-22; 11:22-24). Now He is returning
to His temple. It is a way of affirming that the ancient covenant had been re-established (cf. Ps. 24:7-10).

▣ "His voice was like the sound of many waters" See notes at Ezek. 1:24 and Rev. 1:15; 14:2; 19:6.

▣ "the earth shone with His glory" The VERB (BDB 21, KB 24,
Hiphil PERFECT) is used of the Shekinah Cloud of Glory during the
wilderness wandering period (cf. Exod. 13:21; 14:20). This is part of the Aaronic blessing of Num. 6:25.
It involved God's face (i.e. intimate presence) to shine in/on those whom He fully accepted.

Special Topic: Glory

Special Topic: Shekinah

verses.zh: 其状如从前他来灭城的时候我所见的异象，那异象如我在迦巴鲁河边所见的异象，我就俯伏在地。
verses.en: It was like the vision I saw when he[NOTE:1] came to destroy the city, and the vision I saw by the Kebar River. I threw myself face down.
notes: Heb “I.” The reading is due to the confusion of yod (י, indicating a first person pronoun) and vav (ו, indicating a third person pronoun). A few medieval Hebrew mss, Theodotion’s Greek version, and the Latin Vulgate support a third person pronoun here.
verses.commentary:
43:3 This vision of the manifested glory of YHWH is the same as in the vision that Ezekiel saw in
chapters 1 and 10 (i.e. the portable throne chariot of YHWH).

NASB, NRSV, REB, NET
"when He came"

NKJV, NJB
"when I came"

TEV
"when God came"

The MT has "when I came" (בבאי), but some Hebrew manuscripts (six)
and the Vulgate have "when he came" (בבאו). There is much confusion in Ezekiel
related to the PRONOUNS "I," "you"; "He" and "they."

The UBS Text Project, p. 169, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

▣ "I fell on my face" See notes at Ezek. 1:28 and 3:23.

verses.zh: 耶和华的荣光从朝东的门照入殿中。
verses.en: The glory of the Lord came into the temple by way of the gate that faces east.

verses.zh: 灵将我举起，带入内院，不料，耶和华的荣光充满了殿。
verses.en: Then a wind[NOTE:1] lifted me up and brought me to the inner court; I watched[NOTE:2] the glory of the Lord filling the temple.[NOTE:3]
notes: See note on “wind” in 2:2.
The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
In 1 Kgs 8:10-11 we find a similar event with regard to Solomon’s temple. See also Exod 40:34-35 and Isa 6:4.
verses.commentary:
43:5 "the Spirit lifted me up and brought me" See notes at Ezek. 3:12 and 40:1.

Special Topic: Spirit in the Bible

▣ "the glory of the Lord filled the house" This was like the Shekinah
cloud that came down on Mount Sinai (cf. Exodus 19:16,18,20), the Tabernacle (cf. Exodus 40:34,35), and
Solomon's temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:10,11; 2 Chr. 5:14; 7:1-2). This is another way of showing that YHWH was
present and the covenant was reestablished.

Special Topic: Shekinah

verses.zh: 我听见有一位从殿中对我说话。有一人站在我旁边。
verses.en: I heard someone speaking to me from the temple, while the man was standing beside me.
verses.commentary:
43:6 "I heard one speaking to me from the house" From the next three verses we know it was YHWH Himself
who had just returned from Babylon. This seems to imply that Ezekiel thought this message was for the
post-exilic community. Surely YHWH does not stay in Babylon.

▣ "while a man was standing beside me" This refers to one of the angel guides (cf. Ezek. 40:3-4).

Special Topic: Apocalyptic Literature

▣ "Son of man" See full note at Ezek. 2:1.

verses.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，这是我宝座之地，是我脚掌所踏之地。我要在这里住，在以色列人中直到永远。以色列家和他们的君王必不再玷污我的圣名，就是行邪淫、在锡安的高处葬埋他们君王的尸首，
verses.en: He said to me: “Son of man, this is the place of my throne[NOTE:1] and the place for the soles of my feet,[NOTE:2] where I will live among the people of Israel forever. The house of Israel will no longer profane my holy name, neither they nor their kings, by their spiritual prostitution or by the pillars of their kings set up when they die.[NOTE:3]
notes: God’s throne is mentioned in Isa 6:1 and Jer 3:17.

Heb “by their corpses in their death.” But the term normally translated “corpses” is better understood here as a reference to funeral pillars or funerary offerings. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:583-85, and L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:257.
verses.commentary:
43:7 "the place of My throne" Normally YHWH's throne is in heaven, but since the vision of chapters 1 and
10 (YHWH's portable Throne Chariot, cf. Ezek. 1:26; 10:1), the new temple is both His throne (cf. Jer. 3:17; 14:21; 17:12)
and His footstool (i.e. the space between the Cherubim on the Ark, cf. 1 Chr. 28:2; Ps. 132; 7: Isa. 66:1; Lam. 2:1). Obviously
this is imagery for power and majesty and not meant to be turned into YHWH, the eternal Spirit, actually sitting on a chair/throne!
Even Ps. 45:6 probably refers to the coming Davidic descendant (i.e. Messiah, cf. 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17), not God (see Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 270-271).

Special Topic: Cherubim

Special Topic: Ark of the Covenant

Special Topic: God Described As Human

▣ "the place of the soles of My feet" Although YHWH lived in heaven, His feet were between the Cherubim
(i.e. Jerusalem, Mt. Moriah, cf. Exod. 25:22; Isa. 37:16) above the Ark of the Covenant in the holy of holies (cf. 1 Chr. 28:2; Ps. 99:5; 132:7;
Isa. 60:13). This dedication service of the new temple is very similar to Solomon's in 1 Kings 8 (cf. Isa. 66:1).

▣ "where I will dwell among the sons of Israel" The VERB (BDB 1014, KB 1496, Qal
IMPERFECT) is used so often in Deuteronomy of the place God will cause His name to dwell (cf. Deut. 12:11; 14:23;
16:2,6,11; 26:2). This promise is also found in Ezek. 37:26-27. It goes back to Exod. 25:8 (YHWH gave them a detailed pattern of the tabernacle,
also Exod. 25:9; 29:45-46).

This same covenant language is continued when the coming Messiah is called Emmanuel (i.e. God with us)
in Isa. 7:14 (cf. Matt. 1:23). This is another way of showing that the covenant has been reestablished (cf. Ezek. 16:60-63; 37:24-28).
YHWH is with His people.

Special Topic: Eden

▣ "forever" See Special Topic: Forever ('olam).

▣ "Israel will not defile My holy name" This is a recurrent issue in Ezekiel. YHWH wants His name revealed to the nations,
not profaned among them (cf. Ezek. 20:9,14,22,39; 36:21,22; 39:7; 43:7,8)! Israel was meant to be a kingdom of priests, but they turned
into a kingdom of idolaters! This will change; a new day is coming! There will be no distinction between Jew and Gentile anymore (cf. Eph. 2:11-3:13).
Joel 2:28 has been realized (cf. Acts 2:14-21).

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

Special Topic: "The Name" of YHWH (OT)

▣ "the corpses" This term (BDB 803, KB 910) has several possible meanings.

- the bodies of dead kings in their tombs/monuments in the vicinity of the temple (cf. Lev. 26:30)

- the offering of dead bodies to Molech (same consonants as "king"; see
Special Topic: Molech)

- the place and practice of ancestral idolatry (cf. Ezek. 43:8; 8:3,16)

The parallelism suggests #3.

NASB
"when they die"

NKJV
"on their high places"

NRSV, JPSOA
"at their death"

TEV, NJB, Peshitta
"by burying the corpses of their dead

kings"

REB
"with the monuments raised to dead

kings"

LXX
"the murders of their princes in the

midst of them"

The only difference between the two options is the vowel points of the MT scholars. The
Hebrew consonants are the same. The question is, "Does the context refer to idolatry (cf. Ezek. 5:11; 23:36-45) or
the monuments (stele) of dead sinful kings?" The The IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 726,
suggests:

"These lifeless idols" are probably not corpses but refer to a pagan cult of the dead, similar
to that of Lev. 26:30. Ezekiel probably had in mind a veneration of the spirits of Israel's royal ancestors,
much like a cult of the royal dead at Ugarit. Whether the kings were considered deified at either place
is not clear."

Special Topic: Masoretic Text

verses.zh: 使他们的门槛挨近我的门槛，他们的门框挨近我的门框；他们与我中间仅隔一墙，并且行可憎的事，玷污了我的圣名，所以我发怒灭绝他们。
verses.en: When they placed their threshold by my threshold and their doorpost by my doorpost, with only the wall between me and them, they profaned my holy name by the abominable deeds they committed. So I consumed them in my anger.
verses.commentary:
43:8 "their threshold by My threshold" The IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 726,
has a good explanitory note:

"The statement here in verse 8 corresponds with the description of the Solomonic temple in
1 Kings 6-7. The original temple was built as one element of the entire Solomonic palace complex. Only a
wall separated the temple and palace, and they bordered "threshold to threshold, and doorpost to doorpost."

▣ "abominations" See Special Topic: Abomination (OT)

▣ "So I have consumed them in My anger" See
Special Topic: God Described As Human (anthropomorphism).

verses.zh: 现在他们当从我面前远除邪淫和他们君王的尸首，我就住在他们中间直到永远。
verses.en: Now they must put away their spiritual prostitution and the pillars of their kings far from me, and then I will live among them forever.
verses.commentary:
43:9-11 There is a series of commands.

- put away harlotry, Ezek. 43:9, BDB 934, KB 1221, Piel IMPERFECT used
in a JUSSIVE sense

- describe/declare, Ezek. 43:10, BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- be ashamed of iniquities, Ezek. 43:10, BDB 483, KB 480, Niphal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

- make known to them, Ezek. 43:11, BDB 393, KB 390, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- write, Ezek. 43:11, BDB 507, KB 503, Qal IMPERATIVE

- observe, Ezek. 43:11, BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT used
in a JUSSIVE sense

43:9 "Now let them" Ezek. 43:9, 11 show the conditional nature of Ezekiel's covenant, as most covenants in
the OT were conditional on mankind's appropriate response to God in repentance, faith, obedience, and perseverance.

Special Topic: Covenant

▣ "and I will dwell among them forever" See note at Ezek. 43:7.

verses.zh: 人子啊，你要将这殿指示以色列家，使他们因自己的罪孽惭愧，也要他们量殿的尺寸。
verses.en: “As for you, son of man, describe the temple to the house of Israel, so that they will be ashamed of their sins and measure the pattern.
verses.commentary:
43:10 This elaborate plan of the new temple was meant to

- remind them of the Exodus (a detailed pattern from YHWH of a place of worship and its procedures,
cf. Exodus 25-31; Special Topic: Repentance [OT])

- cause them to repent (cf. Ezek. 6:9; 16:61,63; 20:43; 36:31; 43:11)

- give them an opportunity for obedience (i.e. "and do them," Ezek. 43:11; Special Topic: Keep)

NASB
"let them measure the plan"

NKJV, NRSV
"let them measure the pattern"

TEV
"let them study the plan"

NJB
"(let them draw up the plan of it)"

JPSOA
"let them measure its design"

LXX, RSV, NEB
"and its appearance and plan"

The MT is reflected in the NKJV, NRSV. The UBS Text Project, p. 171, supports the MT over
the LXX, but only with a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

verses.zh: 他们若因自己所行的一切事惭愧，你就将殿的规模、样式、出入之处，和一切形状、典章、礼仪、法则指示他们，在他们眼前写上，使他们遵照殿的一切规模典章去做。
verses.en: When they are ashamed of all that they have done, make known to them the design of the temple—its pattern, its exits and entrances, and its whole design—all its statutes, its entire design, and all its laws; write it all down in their sight, so that they may observe its entire design and all its statutes and do them.
verses.commentary:
43:11 Notice the parallelism between

- design, BDB 849, KB 1017, only in this chapter, possibly drawing, plan, or form

- statutes, BDB 349, cf. Ezek. 43:18

- laws, BDB 435, cf. Ezek. 43:12(twice)

YHWH is giving them a new temple (i.e. to build) and new procedures (i.e. to act on) to test
their obedience. They failed the tabernacle test; they failed Solomon's temple test; they will fail Zerubbabel's
and Herod's tests also! Only after the new covenant of chapter 36 and the restoration of chapter 37 can
Israel be obedient.

Special Topic: Terms for God's Revelation

verses.zh: 殿的法则乃是如此：殿在山顶上，四围的全界要称为至圣。这就是殿的法则。」
verses.en: “This is the law of the temple: The entire area on top of the mountain all around will be most holy. Indeed, this is the law of the temple.

verses.zh: 以下量祭坛，是以肘为度（这肘是一肘零一掌）。底座高一肘，边宽一肘，四围起边高一掌，这是坛的座。
verses.en: “And these are the measurements of the altar:[NOTE:1] Its base[NOTE:2] is 1¾ feet[NOTE:3] high[NOTE:4] and 1¾ feet[NOTE:5] wide, and its border 9 inches[NOTE:6] on its edge. This is to be the height[NOTE:7] of the altar.
notes: Heb “the measurements of the altar by cubits, the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth.” The measuring units here and in the remainder of this section are the Hebrew “long” cubit, consisting of a cubit (about 18 inches or 45 cm) and a handbreadth (about 3 inches or 7.5 cm), for a total of 21 inches (52.5 cm). Because modern readers are not familiar with the cubit as a unit of measurement, and due to the additional complication of the “long” cubit as opposed to the regular cubit, all measurements have been converted to American standard feet and inches, with the Hebrew measurements and the metric equivalents given in the notes. On the altar see Ezek 40:47.
The Hebrew term normally means “bosom.” Here it refers to a hollow in the ground.
Heb “one cubit” (i.e., 52.5 cm).
The word “high” is not in the Hebrew text but is supplied in the translation for clarity.
Heb “one cubit” (i.e., 52.5 cm).
Heb “one span.” A span was three handbreadths, or about 9 inches (i.e., 22.5 cm).
Heb “bulge, protuberance, mound.” The translation follows the LXX.
verses.commentary:
43:13 "cubit" See Special Topic: Cubit

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA, LXX, NET
"height"

REB
"rim"

NJB, Peshitta
"edge"

JPSOA footnote, NET footnote
"bulge"

The MT has "back" (BDB 146; it suggests "anything that is convex").

- back, rim ‒ גב

- height ‒ גבה (KB 170)

The UBS Text Project, p. 173, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

This term relates to the rim of the altar.

verses.zh: 从底座到下层磴台，高二肘，边宽一肘。从小磴台到大磴台，高四肘，边宽一肘。
verses.en: From the base of the ground to the lower ledge is 3½ feet,[NOTE:1] and the width 1¾ feet;[NOTE:2] and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge, 7 feet,[NOTE:3] and the width 1¾ feet;
notes: Heb “2 cubits” (i.e., 1.05 meters).
Heb “one cubit” (i.e., 52.5 cm; the phrase occurs again later in this verse).
Heb “4 cubits” (i.e., 2.1 meters; the phrase also occurs in the next verse).

verses.zh: 坛上的供台，高四肘。供台的四拐角上都有角。
verses.en: and the altar hearth, 7 feet, and from the altar hearth four horns projecting upward.
verses.commentary:
43:15 "and from the altar hearth shall extend upwards four horns" There are numerous references to the
four horns (i.e. like cow horns) of the sacrificial altar in the OT (cf. Exod. 27:2; 29:12; 30:10;
1 Kgs. 1:50; 2:28). Even the incense altar had four horns. This was the most holy part of the sacrificial
altar on which a small portion of the blood was smeared (cf. Exod. 29:12; Lev. 4:7,18,25; 9:9; Ezek. 43:20)
before the rest was poured out at the base of the altar of sacrifice.

Special Topic: Altar of Sacrifice

Special Topic: Altar of Incense

verses.zh: 供台长十二肘，宽十二肘，四面见方。
verses.en: Now the altar hearth[NOTE:1] is a perfect square, 21 feet[NOTE:2] long and 21 feet wide.
notes: The precise Hebrew word used here to refer to an “altar hearth” occurs only here in the OT.
Heb “12 cubits” (i.e., 6.3 meters; the phrase occurs twice in this verse).
verses.commentary:
43:16

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NEt
"altar hearth"

TEV
"the top of the altar"

REB, JPSOA, NJB
"hearth"

LXX, Peshitta
"the altar"

The MT has BDB 72, KB 87 I, which occurs only here in vv. 15,16. KB suggests a related
form which denotes an altar for burnt sacrifices.

verses.zh: 磴台长十四肘，宽十四肘，四面见方。四围起边高半肘，底座四围的边宽一肘。台阶朝东。
verses.en: The ledge is 24½ feet[NOTE:1] long and 24½ feet wide on four sides; the border around it is 10½ inches,[NOTE:2] and its surrounding base 1¾ feet.[NOTE:3] Its steps face east.”
notes: Heb “fourteen”; the word “cubits” is not in the Hebrew text but is understood from the context; the phrase occurs again later in this verse. Fourteen cubits is about 7.35 meters.
Heb “half a cubit” (i.e., 26.25 cm).
Heb “one cubit” (i.e., 52.5 cm).

verses.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，主耶和华如此说：建造祭坛，为要在其上献燔祭洒血，造成的时候典章如下：
verses.en: Then he said to me: “Son of man, this is what the Sovereign Lord says: These are the statutes of the altar: On the day it is built to offer up burnt offerings on it and to sprinkle blood on it,[NOTE:1]
notes: For the “sprinkling of blood,” see Lev 1:5, 11; 8:19; 9:12.
verses.commentary:
43:18 This clearly states that the altar was for the purpose of atonement (i.e. Lev. 1:5,11; 3:2,8,13),
not a memorial (cf. Ezek. 45:15, 17, 20). This is superseded by the NT book of Hebrews (esp. Heb. 9-10), which
sees Jesus as the last sacrifice needed to atone for mankind's sin.

Special Topic: The Superiority of the New Covenant Over the Mosaic Covenant

verses.zh: 主耶和华说，你要将一只公牛犊作为赎罪祭，给祭司利未人撒督的后裔，就是那亲近我、事奉我的。
verses.en: you will give a young bull for a sin offering to the Levitical priests who are descended from Zadok, who approach me to minister to me, declares the Sovereign Lord.
verses.commentary:
43:19 Originally, only the family of Aaron could act as priests serving the altar, but in the post-exilic period there was
not enough of this family to serve so other Levitical families begn to share the task.

Special Topic: Levitical Priests

verses.zh: 你要取些公牛的血，抹在坛的四角和磴台的四拐角，并四围所起的边上。你这样洁净坛，坛就洁净了。
verses.en: You will take some of its blood and place it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge, and on the border all around; you will purify it and make atonement for it.[NOTE:1]
notes: Note the similar language in Lev 16:18.
verses.commentary:
43:20 "cleanse it" This VERB (BDB 306, KB 305, Piel PERFECT with waw)
is repeated in Ezek. 43:22 (twice) and the Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT in Ezek. 43:23. The Piel denotes
cleansing by means of a blood sacrifice (cf. Lev. 8:15; Ezek. 45:18) as does the next VERB "make atonement" (BDB 497, KB 493,
Piel PERFECT with waw, cf. Ezek. 43:26; 45:20). The altar must be inaugurated with a blood sacrifice (cf. Lev. 16:18).
Ezekiel was very familiar with Levitical rituals.

verses.zh: 你又要将那作赎罪祭的公牛犊烧在殿外、圣地之外预定之处。
verses.en: You will also take the bull for the sin offering, and it will be burned in the appointed place in the temple, outside the sanctuary.

verses.zh: 次日，要将无残疾的公山羊献为赎罪祭；要洁净坛，像用公牛犊洁净的一样。
verses.en: “On the second day, you will offer a male goat without blemish for a sin offering. They will purify the altar just as they purified it with the bull.

verses.zh: 洁净了坛，就要将一只无残疾的公牛犊和羊群中一只无残疾的公绵羊
verses.en: When you have finished purifying it, you will offer an unblemished young bull and an unblemished ram from the flock.

verses.zh: 奉到耶和华前。祭司要撒盐在其上，献与耶和华为燔祭。
verses.en: You will present them before the Lord, and the priests will scatter salt on them[NOTE:1] and offer them up as a burnt offering to the Lord.
notes: It is likely that salt was used with sacrificial meals (Num 18:19; 2 Chr 13:5).
verses.commentary:
43:24 "salt" Usually salt was put with the grain offerings (cf. Lev. 2:13) and here with blood offerings.
Because of Ezek. 6:9 it possibly was put on all offerings. It was a symbol of the Israelite's covenant with
YHWH (cf. Num. 18:19; 2 Chr. 13:5).

Special Topic: Salt

verses.zh: 七日内，每日要预备一只公山羊为赎罪祭，也要预备一只公牛犊和羊群中的一只公绵羊，都要没有残疾的。
verses.en: “For seven days you will provide every day a goat for a sin offering; a young bull and a ram from the flock, both without blemish, will be provided.
verses.commentary:
43:25 "for seven days" This purification and dedication procedure parallels Exod. 29:35-37; Lev. 8:33-36.
Holy things had to have a special initiation and also rigid procedures for maintaining their holiness. The
Mosaic legislation (and also that of Ezekiel) was keen on maintaining a strict separation between the holy
and the mundane, the clean and the unclean. This ritual separation reflected their theology of the world
and life, the physical and spiritual.

▣ "goat" Goats were not used in the Mosaic system for dedication offerings.

verses.zh: 七日祭司洁净坛，坛就洁净了；要这样把坛分别为圣。
verses.en: For seven days they will make atonement for the altar and cleanse it, so they will consecrate it.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “fill its hands.”
verses.commentary:
43:26 "so shall they consecrate it" This is literally "fill the hands" (BDB 569, KB 583, Piel
PERFECT with waw; cf. Exod. 29:24).

verses.zh: 满了七日，自八日以后，祭司要在坛上献你们的燔祭和平安祭；我必悦纳你们。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: When the prescribed period is over,[NOTE:1] on the eighth day and thereafter the priests will offer up on the altar your burnt offerings and your peace offerings;[NOTE:2] I will accept you, declares the Sovereign Lord.”
notes: Heb “and they will complete the days.”
The people also could partake of the food of the peace offering (Lev 3).
verses.commentary:
43:27 "peace offering" This was the fellowship meal where God symbolically ate with the offerer
(Leviticus 3). It was eaten in the temple setting and is a foreshadowing of the Lord's Supper.

Special Topic: Peace Offering

▣ "I will accept you, declares the Lord God" This was the purpose of
Ezekiel's sacrificial cultus (i.e. reunite sinful national Israel with their holy God). Ezekiel sees it in terms of ancient sacrificial
ritual (i.e. Leviticus 1-7). Remember, he was a trained priest.

The VERB (BDB 953, KB 1280, Qal PERFECT) is also used in Ezek.
20:40,41 of an accepted sacrifice. Because YHWH was with His people, purity, holiness, ceremonial cleanness must be maintained!
